preRules.note: A noncharacter U+FDD0-U+FDDF in the text is not one of the tables' marks: U+FFFD, passed through and reported.
ై is ె + ౖ (its canonical decomposition): the composer writes the e-shape of the letter and the length mark 4F (కై = 4D F0 FC 4F).
క్ష్మ is క + the combined vattu 87 (క్ష్మి = 4D EC FC 87); with ై it is క్ష + ్మ (84 F0 FC 95 C3).
క్ష is one letter: 84 E6 FC (U+FDD2 marks it).
A virama before a ZWJ: the fonts have no half forms; drawn as the visible halant, as before a ZWNJ.
No face has a subjoined ఝ (the composer drops ఝ after the link): the visible halant of the letter before it, then ఝ in full.
స్త్ర: స + the combined ్త్ర glyph 88 (E7 DC 88), no hook.
ష్ట్ర: ష + the combined ్ట్ర glyph 89 (E7 D9 89), no hook.

A virama with no consonant after it (at a word end, before a space, punctuation or a sign) is the visible halant: the composer's spelling of C + ్ + ZWNJ (క్‌ = 4D 8A FC). Its pending link writes the bare letter, losing the virama (tools/Shared/ShreeWordFinal.cs).
The ra-vattu with ై: the deeper hook 5B before the cluster (క్రై = 5B 4D F0 FC 4F).
The ra-vattu is the hook 7B BEFORE its cluster, where the composer writes it (క్ర = 7B 4D E6 FC, క్క్ర = 7B 4D E6 FC 50; U+FDD3 marks it).
Once more, for a second ra-vattu in one cluster (not well-formed text): a hook too, so no virama is left over.
A vowel sign (or the visible halant) on a cluster shapes its first letter; the subjoined letters follow (క్కి = 4D EC FC 50). ృ stays after them.
The ై mark is 95 before the wide vattu of ఖ గ ఘ ఙ జ ఞ ట ఠ డ ఢ ణ త థ ద ధ ల ష (ఖ్ఖై = 52 F1 FD 95 55).
After క్ష with no sign of its own (or with ై) a narrow vattu follows the spacer A0 (క్ష్క = 84 E6 FC A0 50, క్ష్కై = 84 F0 FC 95 A0 50; క్ష్కి = 84 EC FC 50).
After క్ష (with any sign but ొ ో) a wide vattu follows the wide spacer 9B (క్ష్ఖ = 84 E6 FC 9B 55, క్ష్ఖి = 84 EC FC 9B 55; క్ష్ఖొ = 84 F6 55).
ృ after a vattu, or after క్ష: the spacer A0 before it (క్కృ = 4D E6 FC 50 A0 96, క్షృ = 84 E6 FC A0 96).
ASCII " that opens a quote (at the start, after a space, a bracket or a dash) is “, two ‘ (22 22).
Any other ASCII " closes a quote: ”, two ’ (27 27).
ASCII ' that opens a quote is ‘ (22).
Any other ASCII ' (a closing quote, an apostrophe) is ’ (27).

postRules.note: U+FDD1 marks what draws nothing (a joiner) and keeps a pair's codes apart; it is not text.
